size.note: Newman's 54–60 cm. Wikipedia 52–60 cm. Wingspan: Wikipedia gives 130–150 cm. Mass: Newman's Birds gives 0.4–1 kg.

habitat: Woodland and forest edge where wasp/bee nests are available; Palearctic non-breeding visitor (Newman's; SABAP1).

distribution.note: GBIF records per 10 000 bird records in each region: far north 0.57, north 0.22, central 0.27, south 0.42 (counted 13 November 2026). Recorded most often in the far north.

summary: Buzzard-sized but small-headed with a longish neck and pigeon-like face. Plumage highly variable (pale to dark); typically barred underparts and a banded tail. Specialises on wasp larvae (Newman's; Wikipedia).

similar.note: Common/Steppe Buzzard has a larger head, shorter neck and different underwing pattern; Honey Buzzard looks small-headed in flight (Newman's).

calls.description: Seldom calls in Africa non-breeding grounds; whistling calls on breeding grounds (Wikipedia).

research.note: Research confidence was medium-high and is stored as medium. Status is stored as palearctic-migrant. The European Honey Buzzard is a Palearctic summer visitor. No seasonal plumage change is described in the sources consulted, except presence/absence of migrants. Colour phrases outside the vocabulary were stored as the nearest swatch: dark to dark-brown.
